en: Now follows the *Gaṅgāṣṭaka* composed by the illustrious Vālmīki.
O Mother, rival of the Daughter of the Mountain, the pearl-necklace adorning the peak of the earth,
the victory banner for the ascent to heaven— I pray to you, Bhāgīrathī.
May I dwell upon your banks, drink your waters, and swing upon your waves.
While remembering your name and fixing my gaze upon you, may the destruction of my body come to pass. || 1 ||

O Gaṅgā, destroyer of hell, it is better for a bird to dwell within the hollow of a tree on your bank than for a king— whose fame is praised by all his enemies' wives— to be elsewhere, amidst the ringing of bells from the clash of herds of elephants blinded by rut.
May I be a bull, a bird, a horse, a serpent, or some elephant that is unconfined, unable to endure the suffering and pain of birth and death;
but never again may I be a king, fanned by the breezes of chowries from courtesans, with the sound of tinkling bells as my only companion. || 3 ||

When, being fanned by the breezes from the beautiful whisks in the hands of celestial maidens, shall I be— once torn apart by crows, devoured by dogs, scavenged by jackals, washed away by the currents, tossed by the waters of the bank, and rocked by the waves?
O Supreme Goddess, O Bhāgīrathī who flows through the three paths, I shall behold your own form.
This garland of *mālatī* flowers upon the head of Viṣṇu— the destroyer of Madana, whose lotus feet are like fresh sprouts of the poison-creeper—
is some kind of victory banner of the Goddess of Liberation; may it be triumphant!
May the Jahnavi, who has washed away the stain of strife, purify us. || 5 ||

May the pure water of the Gaṅgā be for my daily bathing—water that possesses parasols formed by the swaying creepers and vines of the tāla, tamāla, sāla, and sarala trees; that is free from the scorching heat of the sun’s rays; that is as brilliant as a conch shell, the moon, and jasmine flowers; and that is embraced by the high breasts of the wives of gandharvas, gods, siddhas, and kinnaras. || 6 ||
May the enchanting water of the Gaṅgā, fallen from the feet of Murāri, flowing upon the head of Tripurāri, and destroying sins, purify me. (7)

May the water of the Ganges— which removes evil, destroys misfortune, bears upon its waves, flows over the mountains, bursts forth from the caves of the king of mountains, produces a humming sound, carries the dust of Hari’s feet, and constantly brings about auspiciousness— purify us forever.

The man who, being self-restrained, recites at dawn this auspicious *Gaṅgāṣṭaka* composed by Vālmīki, quickly washes away the mud of the body’s sins and misdeeds, attains liberation, and that person shall never again fall into the ocean of worldly existence. 9.
Thus ends the Gaṅgāṣṭaka composed by Vālmīki.
